theme: Agent 怎麼管理自己的記憶與 context——訓練記憶決策、檢驗知識圖假設、決定工具輸出保留比例
notes: Announcement batch confirmed via arxiv.org/list/{cat}/new page headers: Tuesday, 1 September 2026 (cs.AI IDs 2608.28590-2608.31137, cs.CL IDs 2608.28608-~2608.29865+, cs.MA new submissions 2608.28658-2608.30938). Groundlane web_search returned almost no same-day candidates (fresh preprints not yet indexed), so full title lists were pulled directly via web_extract on arxiv.org/list/{cat}/new (div.list-title + dt selectors) across paginated batches, then screened by title/abstract.

Data-integrity issue caught during screening: a two-array (titles[] / ids[]) extraction from the cs.CL listing page desynchronized partway through (mismatched dt/div.list-title counts), which initially mis-paired two candidate titles ('Agent Zero Memory', 'Hindsight Memory-PRM') with wrong arxiv IDs. Caught by fetching the returned abs page and finding the title did not match; corrected by re-resolving both titles via the arXiv API's ti: exact-title search (export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=ti:"..."), which returned the correct IDs 2608.29606 and 2608.29605 respectively. All final selected/rejected IDs below were independently confirmed by fetching their own arxiv.org/abs/{id} or arxiv.org/html/{id}v1 page and checking the returned title matches.

A strong 'agent memory/context management' cluster emerged independently across cs.AI, cs.CL and cs.MA in this batch (at least 8 distinct memory-related papers: TRACER, Selective Forgetting, Agent Zero Memory, Hindsight Memory-PRM, MedCache, From-Extraction-to-Governed-Memory, Not-All-or-None memory graph, Conditional Memory Adapters). Three were selected for angle diversity (train-the-manager / test-the-structural-assumption / in-session-retention) and evidence rigor; two comparable 'new SOTA long-term memory system' papers on the same benchmarks (Agent Zero Memory vs Hindsight Memory-PRM) were both read in full text, and only the more rigorously controlled one was selected to avoid redundant framing.

Full method, experiment, baseline, and limitation sections were read (not abstract-only) via arxiv.org/html/{id}v1 for all three selected papers, and for Agent Zero Memory before it was set to watch/rejected-for-redundancy.

candidates.title: Hindsight Memory-PRM: Supervising Memory Management with Auditable Hindsight Credit
credibilityEvidence: Table 1 (S4.2): same-scaffold controlled comparison (fixed backbone/retriever, only the memory manager varies) plus a separate system-level reference row for Mem0's official operating point.
3-seed standard deviation reported for all same-scaffold arms; LoCoMo per-dialogue block-permutation sign test p=0.031 (Appendix K).

2x2 factorial ablation (S4.5) isolating critic vs. audited-term contributions (6.0 / 7.6 points, +0.5 interaction); critic validity section (S4.4) with deletion-causality test (top-scored -9.6 vs random -2.1 vs bottom-scored -0.8) and adversarial false-positive rate 3.2%.
Explicit Limitations section (S4.8): schema must be hand-designed per domain, forgetting under-stressed (LoCoMo has no overturned facts), probe generation bound to one closed-source model.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Two public long-term-memory benchmarks, controlled same-scaffold baselines, a 2x2 ablation, critic-validity checks, reward-erosion controls, and a transfer-diagnosis experiment together support the causal claim that intervention-calibrated credit (not just denser observational signal) drives the gain; the paper itself scopes the claim away from deletion-heavy/forgetting scenarios.
reproducibilityEvidence: Full algorithm, loss terms, and hyperparameter search ranges given in the paper and appendices
No public code/checkpoint/dataset release link found in the fetched full text
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The claim 'local 8B manager surpasses its API teacher and a budget-matched/official Mem0 baseline at 1/8th context' is backed by multiple independent controlled comparisons and ablations, not a single headline number.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Storage schema requires manual per-domain design; the reward/credit design has not been stress-tested under scenarios requiring active forgetting of overturned facts.
candidates.presentationReason: Method, reward formulation, baselines, ablations, and limitations are explicitly separated and each backed by a specific experiment.
candidates.reason: Most rigorously controlled of several same-day memory-management papers: reproduces baselines under a shared scaffold, isolates credit-assignment mechanism via ablation, and validates the learned critic causally rather than only correlationally.

candidates.title: Selective Forgetting: A Graph-Based Memory Framework for Long-Term LLM Agents
credibilityEvidence: Matched-budget comparison (5 retrieval roots) between graph memory and a flat vector baseline on LongMemEval, with a paired bootstrap over 500 questions: token F1 0.417 vs 0.468, Delta=-0.050, 95% CI [-0.085,-0.016].
Breakdown by question category showing the largest gap on prior-assistant-turn recall questions (0.911 -> 0.607 judged correctness).

Forgetting-module ablation on a persistent 27,021-node graph: removes 9.8% of nodes / 9.5% of bytes with token F1 change +0.001 (95% CI [-0.015,+0.016]) and correctness change -1.6 points (95% CI upper bound +0.006, i.e. loss bounded at 3.8 points).
Authors explicitly scope the claim in the abstract: single small extractor model, one benchmark, describes 'this extraction-based pipeline rather than graph-structured memory in general'.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Statistically well-supported for the narrow claim tested (this pipeline, one benchmark, one extractor), but authors themselves disclaim generalization to graph-structured agent memory as a category.
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The narrow, author-scoped claim ('this graph pipeline does not beat matched-budget flat retrieval on LongMemEval') is directly supported by confidence intervals; editorial framing must preserve that scope rather than generalize to all graph memory.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Single small extractor model evaluated on a single benchmark; cannot rule out that the negative result is specific to this implementation rather than graph-structured memory broadly.
candidates.presentationReason: Claim, evidence, and explicit scope-narrowing are stated together in the abstract and carried through the results section.
candidates.reason: Rare same-day negative-result paper directly testing (rather than assuming) a widely adopted design choice in agent memory systems, with full statistical rigor and open code; provides an evaluation/limits counterweight to the two method papers in the same cluster.

candidates.title: TRACER: Per-Tool Context Retention for LLM Agents via Consequence-Attributed Reinforcement Learning
credibilityEvidence: Production deployment evaluation (data-analysis agent at an unnamed large e-commerce company), 120 human-verified production queries split 80 train / 40 held-out, 5 seeds, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, 95% CIs.
Tested across three compressor backends plus a held-out fourth (AGORA-style) for cross-compressor transfer; also tested transfer across agent backbones and on 5 held-out LOCA-bench environments.
Learned outcome-model attributor validated on held-out episodes: Spearman rho=0.72 for per-tool re-invocation prediction, Brier score 0.07 for success prediction.
Iso-success token-ratio metric used to avoid confounding token savings with task failure; ablates against uniform/recency/token-proportional/tool-type-conditional baselines.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Methodologically rigorous (seeds, significance tests, cross-backbone/compressor transfer) but the held-out test set is small (40 queries) from a single company's single agent stack; no external replication is possible since the deployment and data are proprietary.
reproducibilityEvidence: Uses internal production logs and an internally deployed agent stack
No public dataset, code, or checkpoint link found in the fetched text
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The core token-savings-without-success-loss claim is statistically tested, but generalization beyond one company's tool ecosystem is unverified and the company/paper affiliation itself is not disclosed.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Single-company, single-deployment validation with no public code or data for external replication.
candidates.presentationReason: Problem framing (compression-consequence gap), method, and experimental setup are explicit; baselines and metrics are clearly defined.
candidates.reason: Distinct angle from the other two (in-session tool-output retention vs. cross-session long-term memory), with a real production deployment and a credit-assignment design (learned per-tool counterfactual attributor) directly applicable to enterprise tool-use agent platforms.

candidates.title: Agent Zero Memory: Provenance-Aware Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents
credibilityEvidence: Reports new SOTA on LongMemEval (95.60%) and LoCoMo (93.60%), margins of +0.73 and +1.10 points over the next-best system (Mastra, Mem0), per Tables 3-4.
8-backbone controlled cost/latency/accuracy study (Table 5-6) and a retrieval-channel ablation (Table 7) are genuinely controlled experiments by the authors.

However, the headline SOTA comparison table itself compares against competitor systems' own self-reported numbers (Mastra, Hindsight/Vectorize, EmergenceMem, Supermemory, Zep, Mem0, ByteRover 2.0), not a reproduction under one shared protocol, and no variance/significance test is reported for the main SOTA margins (0.73/1.10 points).
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: The backbone/ablation studies are solid, but the headline SOTA claim rests on small point-estimate margins against externally self-reported leaderboard numbers with no reported confidence interval or significance test.
reproducibilityEvidence: No public code/data release link found in the fetched full text (company paper, Zero Labs)
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Backbone-agnostic design claims are well supported; the 'new SOTA' framing itself is less rigorously supported than Hindsight Memory-PRM's same-scaffold comparisons.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Main competitor comparison uses externally self-reported numbers rather than a controlled reproduction, with no variance reporting on the small headline margins.
candidates.presentationReason: Extensive related-work table and formal definitions make design choices and comparison scope easy to follow.
candidates.reason: Strong systems paper but overlaps heavily with selected Hindsight Memory-PRM (same two benchmarks, same 'new long-term memory system' framing) with comparatively weaker comparison rigor; held back to avoid redundant angle and to watch for an updated version with controlled baseline reproduction or significance testing.

candidates.title: From Extraction to Governed Memory: Multi-Agent Knowledge Graph Construction with Domain-Expert Review
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Abstract-level screen only; not selected due to angle overlap and narrower scope, so full-text credibility check was not performed.
candidates.reason: Domain-specific knowledge-graph construction pipeline with human-in-the-loop review; framed around a one-off KG build rather than ongoing agent memory management, lower today-importance than the three selected memory-management papers.

candidates.title: MedCache: Efficient and Temporally Valid Memory for Longitudinal Clinical Agents
candidates.reason: Clinical-vertical-specific memory system; narrower practical link for a general Agent-engineering readership than the three selected cross-domain papers.

candidates.title: Localizing Emergent Failures in Agentic AI: Recovering Minimal Repair Families via Counterfactual Replay
candidates.reason: Interesting agent-failure-repair direction (also cross-listed under cs.MA), but belongs to a different cluster (failure attribution, not memory/context management); the memory cluster had stronger same-day depth and cohesion, so this was left for a future digest rather than forced into today's theme.
